sections.markdown:
## C2 — Warning signs, other sign types and sign confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A22
Warning signs give road users notice of a situation that may not be easy to see in time. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A22
Some warning signs announce a control device before you reach it, such as Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead and Signal Ahead. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A22
Warning signs also flag the shape of the road, including a sharp right turn, curves, sharp turns, a steep hill and a side road entering ahead. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A22
Other warning signs tell you that lanes or roads are changing: a lane ends and you merge left, two roads merge, the road divides ahead, or a divided road ends ahead. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A22
Intersection warnings in the manual include a general intersection sign, a "T" intersection ahead, a traffic circle or roundabout, and a railroad before a "T" intersection. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A22
Crossing warnings cover pedestrians, trails, pedestrians with bicycles, trucks, and deer or other wildlife. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F40 | anchor: A22
The warning sign set in the manual also shows a Slippery When Wet sign and a No Passing Zone sign. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F41 | anchor: A22
School warnings include a School Crossing Ahead sign and a School Bus Stop Ahead sign. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F42 | anchor: A22
Work-area warnings include Flagger Ahead, Roadwork Ahead, Detour, Begin Work Zone and End Active Work Zone. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F43 | anchor: A22
A sign stating that a work zone is active when its lights flash is labeled in the manual with a note that fines are increased. [A22]
Why it matters: a flashing work-zone sign signals higher fines, so slow down and obey the zone limits.
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec05-F44 | anchor: A23
Overhead lane use signs are mounted above the road and tell you about destinations, directions and how to use each lane. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-F45 | anchor: A23
Some roads carry route numbers, and route marker signs show both the route number and the kind of road, such as a U.S. route or a state route. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-F46 | anchor: A23
Service information and guide signs tell you which businesses and services you can reach by taking certain exits. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-F47 | anchor: A23
Examples of service and guide signs in the manual point to lodging, a hospital, gas, food, an airport, a train station and a park and ride lot. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-F48 | anchor: A23
Mile marker signs stand at every mile along interstate highways. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-F49 | anchor: A23
A mile marker tells you where you are, so you can guide a tow truck or emergency personnel to your location. [A23]
Why it matters: note the nearest mile marker when you call for help on an interstate.
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A21
The stop sign is the only 8-sided sign and uses white letters on red, while the yield sign is the only 3-sided sign and uses red letters on white. [A21]
Why it matters: group_hint stop-yield; prereq_hint sec05-F13; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F23, sec05-F26.
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A20
An octagon always demands a complete stop, whereas a triangle asks you to slow down and stop only if needed to give others the right-of-way. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint stop-yield; prereq_hint sec05-R01; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F13, sec05-F14.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A20
A round sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead, while a crossbuck marks the crossing location itself. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint railroad-signs; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F19, sec05-F20.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A20
Yellow is a general warning, orange warns of construction or maintenance work, and fluorescent yellow-green is reserved for school, pedestrian and bicycle signs. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint sec05-F02; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F04, sec05-F06, sec05-F10.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A20
Green guides you with destinations, distances and directions, blue points to services, and brown marks recreation and cultural interest areas. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint sign-colors; prereq_hint sec05-F02; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F07, sec05-F08, sec05-F09.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A20
A diamond warns of hazards ahead, a pennant marks the start of a no passing zone, and a pentagon signals a school zone or school crossing. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint sign-shapes; prereq_hint sec05-F01; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F15, sec05-F16, sec05-F18.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A20
A vertical rectangle usually gives a rule or instruction, while a horizontal rectangle usually gives directions or information. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint sign-shapes; prereq_hint sec05-F17; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F17, sec05-F21.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A21
A Two-way Left sign lets traffic from both directions use the center lane for left turns, while a One Way sign allows travel only in the arrow's direction. [A21]
Why it matters: group_hint lane-regulation; prereq_hint sec05-F22; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F31, sec05-F32.
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0021]
